question.prompt: The sides of triangle \(BAC\) are in the ratio \(2:3:4.\) \(BD\) is the angle-bisector drawn to the shortest side \(AC,\) dividing it into segments \(AD\) and \(CD.\) If the length of \(AC\) is \(10,\) then the length of the longer segment of \(AC\) is:

solutions.explanation:
Because \(AC\) is the shortest side, it corresponds to the \(2\) in the ratio \(2:3:4\). Thus the other two sides, \(AB\) and \(BC\), have ratio \(3:4\), in some order.

The internal angle bisector theorem gives
\[
\frac{AD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{BC}.
\]
Therefore the two pieces of \(AC\) also have ratio \(3:4\), in some order. Their total length is \(10\), representing \(3+4=7\) equal shares. The longer piece contains four shares, so its length is
\[
10\cdot\frac47=\frac{40}{7}=\boxed{5\frac57},
\]
choice C.
solutions.title: Divide the side in the adjacent-side ratio
